title: Stocks Slide at the Open as Alphabet Drags Tech; GDP Beats Forecast at 3.4%
dek: The Dow was down 0.33% at 10:48 AM ET and the Nasdaq had fallen about 1.2% in early trading, as Alphabet's results and AI-spending worries outweighed a stronger-than-expected GDP print.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Federal Reserve Building in Washington, D.C.

keyPoints: The Dow Jones Industrial Average was 52,300.08, down 175.02 points or 0.33%, as of 10:48:40 AM ET, per Yahoo Finance.
Early in the session the Nasdaq Composite fell about 1.2% and the S&P 500 about 0.3%; CNBC reported at its 10:56 AM ET update that the Nasdaq was down 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.5% just after the open.
The advance Q3 GDP estimate showed 3.4% annualized growth, above the 3.1% Dow Jones consensus, with business investment up 12.7%.
September PCE inflation rose 3.6% year over year and core PCE rose 3.1%, both in line with expectations, keeping December rate-hike odds high.
body:
U.S. stocks opened lower on Thursday, with the tech-heavy indexes leading the decline. Yahoo Finance reported at 10:48:40 AM ET that the Dow Jones Industrial Average stood at 52,300.08, down 175.02 points or 0.33%, and CNBC reported the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.5% just after the open, with the Dow off 0.6%. The moves were early and could change through the session.

The main drag was Alphabet. Bloomberg reported that Alphabet fell 13% as of 9:34 AM ET after a sales miss, while Yahoo Finance said cloud growth of 103% was not enough to offset investor concern about free cash flow and the return on AI spending. A sell-off spread through AI-linked names: Yahoo Finance said the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell and software stocks (IGV) slid, with double-digit losses for Fortinet and ServiceNow after their reports.

The economic data was mixed in tone. The Commerce Department's advance estimate put third-quarter GDP growth at 3.4% annualized, beating the 3.1% consensus and up from 2.2% in the second quarter, according to Yahoo Finance's report of the release. Business investment rose 12.7%, which Yahoo attributed to the AI build-out, and consumer spending grew 3.8%. The PCE price index rose 3.6% year over year in September, and core PCE rose 3.1%, both in line with expectations.

Those prints keep the Federal Reserve in focus. The central bank held rates unchanged on Wednesday on a 10-2 vote with two dissents favoring a hike. Investopedia reported CME FedWatch pricing an 84% likelihood of at least a quarter-point increase at the December meeting.

Oil and rates were also in the mix. Investopedia reported WTI crude futures down 2.2% to $100.47 a barrel and Brent down 1.9% to $109.56, after a Wall Street Journal report of a U.S. letter seeking to restart Iran peace talks. The 10-year Treasury yield was around 4.98%, down from late Wednesday, and gold futures slipped 0.4% to $4,035 an ounce.

What to watch: Amazon and Intel report after the close, and the index moves above should be checked against the closing numbers before drawing a full-day conclusion.

marketImpact.summary: The open shows a tech-led pullback rather than a broad sell-off: Alphabet and AI-linked names are weighing on the Nasdaq while the stronger GDP print supports the economy but reinforces the case for a Fed hike.
marketImpact.timeframe: Through Thursday's close and the after-hours Amazon and Intel reports

tickers.rationale: Down about 13% as of 9:34 AM ET per Bloomberg after a sales miss and free-cash-flow concerns.
Semiconductor ETF fell as AI hardware names sold off with the broader tech group.
Down about 1.4% in early trading per Investopedia, despite a beat on the top and bottom lines.
10-year yield around 4.98% with December hike odds near 84%.
